title.en: USWOO Goes National: New Los Angeles Office and Rental Services Expanding to Chicago, D.C. and Philadelphia
title.zh: USWOO 走向全美：洛杉矶新办公室启用，租赁服务拓展至芝加哥、华盛顿特区和费城

summary.en: After years of supporting renters in New York and New Jersey, USWOO is opening a Los Angeles office and bringing its rental services to three more cities.
summary.zh: 在多年服务纽约和新泽西租客之后，USWOO 将开设洛杉矶办公室，并把租赁服务带到另外三座城市。

body.en:
USWOO today announced its national expansion: a new office in Los Angeles, and rental services now extending to Chicago, Washington, D.C. and Philadelphia.

USWOO began as leasing support for international students and young professionals starting out in New York. As more of those renters moved on to new campuses, jobs and cities, the questions followed them: where to live, how to sign a lease from far away, and who to call once the keys are in hand.

One rental journey, in more cities

In each new city, renters can expect the same support USWOO is known for: home search and tours, application and lease guidance, move-in planning, and everyday help after move-in, with renewal and relocation support when it is time for what comes next.

The new Los Angeles office will be the base for the West Coast, working alongside local partners and neighborhood experts. Renters in Chicago, D.C. and Philadelphia will be supported by the USWOO team together with trusted partners in each city.

Guides to help you choose

To help renters get to know each city before they arrive, USWOO’s City Guides cover popular neighborhoods, nearby schools and everyday essentials across all of our cities.

Looking ahead

“Moving somewhere new shouldn’t mean starting over,” is the idea behind the expansion. USWOO will keep growing city by city, with the same goal everywhere: making the move from finding a home to feeling at home a little easier.

Explore City Guides →
body.zh:
USWOO 今日宣布走向全美：在洛杉矶开设新办公室，并将租赁服务拓展至芝加哥、华盛顿特区和费城。

USWOO 最初是为在纽约起步的国际学生和年轻职场人提供租房支持。随着越来越多租客前往新的校园、工作和城市，同样的问题也跟着他们：住哪里、如何远程签约，拿到钥匙后又该找谁。

同一段租房旅程覆盖更多城市

在每一座新城市，租客都能获得 USWOO 一贯的支持：找房与看房、申请与签约指导、入住规划，以及入住后的日常帮助，并在需要续租或搬家时提供后续支持。

全新的洛杉矶办公室将作为西海岸的据点，与当地合作伙伴和社区专家携手合作。芝加哥、华盛顿特区和费城的租客，则由 USWOO 团队与各城市值得信赖的合作伙伴共同支持。

帮你做选择的城市指南

为了让租客在抵达前就了解每座城市，USWOO 城市指南涵盖我们所有城市的热门社区、周边学校和日常生活必备信息。

展望未来

“搬到新的地方，不该意味着一切从零开始”，这正是此次扩张背后的理念。USWOO 将继续一座城市一座城市地成长，目标始终如一：让从找到房子到住出家的感觉，这段路更轻松一点。

探索城市指南 →

title.en: USWOO Sponsors NYU Stern Real Estate Club’s “Powering the Future” Real Estate Summit
title.zh: USWOO 携手 NYU Stern 支持纽约房地产行业前沿峰会

summary.en: Alongside JLL, Corcoran Sunshine and Naftali Group, USWOO supports Powering the Future, connecting global business perspectives with the next generation of industry talent.
summary.zh: 与 JLL、Corcoran Sunshine、Naftali Group 等行业知名机构共同支持 Powering the Future，连接全球商业视野与新一代行业人才。

body.en:
On March 6, 2026, USWOO, as a sponsor, supported Powering the Future, the annual real estate summit hosted by the NYU Stern Real Estate Club.

The summit brought together professionals from leading global companies and real estate organizations, including IBM, Microsoft, McKinsey and CBRE, to discuss artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, energy systems and the future of cities.

USWOO appeared alongside JLL, Goodwin, Corcoran Sunshine and Naftali Group in the summit’s sponsor lineup, reflecting our close ties to New York’s real estate industry.

Standing alongside industry leaders to explore the future of real estate

Real estate is going through profound change.

From AI-driven energy systems to data center investment and the rethinking of urban space, the links between technology, capital and real estate have never been tighter.

The summit brought global companies, industry experts and the next generation of talent together, moving ideas out of reports and research and into face-to-face conversation.

For USWOO, taking part in an event like this is more than brand visibility. It is an important chance to go deeper into the industry and build professional networks.

From rental services to industry connections

As a brand focused on residential leasing and real estate marketing in the U.S., USWOO pays close attention to market shifts and how urban development shapes where people choose to live.

At the summit, USWOO presented our three core business areas: Rental Solutions, Real Estate Brokerage, and Marketing & Branding.

From serving international students and young professionals to connecting developers, property management companies and industry partners, USWOO continues to expand its professional services and industry network.

We believe valuable service is about more than helping clients find the right home. It also depends on a deep understanding of the market, the accumulation of professional resources, and the ability to keep creating meaningful connections.

Connecting with New York’s industry resources and future talent

New York brings together some of the world’s leading financial institutions, real estate firms, technology companies and universities, and it continues to produce new ideas and opportunities that reshape the industry.

By supporting professional organizations such as the NYU Stern Real Estate Club, USWOO hopes to strengthen its connections with universities, industry organizations and the next generation of real estate professionals, opening the door to more exchange and collaboration.

Rooted in New York, connected to the industry, and ready for more possibilities.

Going forward, USWOO will keep taking part in industry events with real impact, deepen our professional partnerships, and explore more ways real estate can connect with city life.
body.zh:
2026 年 3 月 6 日，USWOO 美窝作为赞助方，支持由 NYU Stern Real Estate Club 举办的年度房地产行业峰会 Powering the Future。

本届峰会汇聚来自 IBM、Microsoft、McKinsey、CBRE 等全球知名企业及房地产行业机构的专业人士，围绕人工智能、数字基础设施、能源系统与未来城市发展展开交流。

USWOO 与 JLL、Goodwin、Corcoran Sunshine、Naftali Group 等行业机构共同出现在本届峰会的赞助阵容中，进一步展现了品牌与纽约房地产行业的紧密联系。

与行业领先者同行，探索房地产的未来

房地产行业正在经历深刻变革。

从 AI 驱动的能源系统，到数据中心投资与城市空间的重新规划，科技、资本与房地产之间的联系正变得前所未有的紧密。

本届峰会将全球企业、行业专家与新一代人才汇聚一堂，让前沿观点走出报告与研究，成为面对面的行业交流。

对 USWOO 而言，参与这样的行业盛会，不仅是一次品牌展示，更是深入行业生态、拓展专业合作网络的重要机会。

从租赁服务到行业连接

作为专注于美国住宅租赁与房地产营销的服务品牌，USWOO 始终关注市场变化，以及城市发展如何影响人们的居住选择。

在峰会现场，USWOO 展示了品牌的三大业务方向：Rental Solutions、Real Estate Brokerage、Marketing & Branding。

从服务国际学生与年轻职场人士，到连接开发商、物业管理公司及行业合作伙伴，USWOO 正在持续拓展自身的专业服务与行业网络。

我们相信，真正有价值的服务，不仅在于帮助客户找到合适的住所，更在于对市场的理解、专业资源的积累，以及持续创造连接的能力。

持续连接纽约的行业资源与未来人才

纽约汇聚了全球领先的金融机构、房地产企业、科技公司与高校，也孕育着持续改变行业的新观点与新机会。

通过支持 NYU Stern Real Estate Club 等专业组织，USWOO 希望进一步加强与高校、行业机构及新一代专业人才的联系，让更多交流与合作成为可能。

立足纽约，连接行业，拓展更多可能。

未来，USWOO 将继续参与具有行业影响力的交流活动，深化专业合作，探索房地产与城市生活的更多可能。

title.en: Studying at NYU, and ending up renting in New Jersey
title.zh: 在 NYU 读书最后却把家租到了 New Jersey

summary.en: From insisting on Manhattan to discovering Jersey City, Ethan’s first off-campus lease changed how he thought about commuting and living in New York.
summary.zh: 从坚持住在 Manhattan，到意外发现 Jersey City，Ethan 的第一次校外租房，彻底改变了他对纽约通勤和居住的认知。

body.en:
Before the end of their freshman year, Ethan and his friend had already started planning to move out of the NYU dorms.

Their plan seemed simple: find an apartment in Manhattan, split the rent, and stay as close to campus as possible.

After weeks of searching, reality turned out harsher than expected.

Apartments within budget were either too small or in poor condition. When they finally found one they liked, it was already rented out before they could book a viewing.

Worse still, rent was only the beginning. Utilities, internet and move-in costs added up to much more than they had budgeted each month.

As the dorm checkout date drew closer, they still hadn’t decided which neighborhood to live in.

“Just because you study in New York, do you have to live in New York?”

After contacting USWOO, the agent didn’t send a pile of listings right away. Instead, they asked about their budget, class schedules and commuting habits.

At the end of the conversation, the agent suddenly asked: “Have you considered Jersey City?”

Ethan’s first reaction was to say no. “I go to school in New York. Why would I live in New Jersey?”

But when the agent put listings in Manhattan and Jersey City side by side, comparing prices and transit routes, he began to waver.

It turned out that from some PATH stations in Jersey City, getting to Manhattan wasn’t nearly as complicated as he had imagined.

And at a similar budget, they might be able to find a more spacious apartment with better amenities.

He had thought he was choosing between budget and comfort, but there was a third option he hadn’t considered.

What changed his mind was the viewing

On the weekend, Ethan and his friend decided to visit Jersey City in person.

Walking out of the PATH station and into several apartment buildings they had never looked at before, they realized that life across the river was very different from what they had imagined.

Bright common spaces, a gym, and some apartments with views of the Manhattan skyline.

Of course, the agent also reminded them not to judge a place by looks alone.

How long was the walk from the apartment to PATH? Was it easy to get home at night? After factoring in transportation costs, how much could they actually save each month?

After comparing several listings and complete commuting routes, they finally chose an apartment near a PATH station.

Not because it was the most luxurious, but because budget, commute and living conditions finally struck the balance they wanted.

Living in New York and living in New York are two different things

After moving to Jersey City, Ethan still went to NYU for class as usual, and spent weekends with friends in Manhattan.

The only difference was that on the way home each day, he could see the familiar New York skyline across the river.

A few months earlier, he had thought living in New Jersey was a compromise.

Looking back now, he is actually glad someone asked him a question at the time:

“Why does it have to be Manhattan?”

Sometimes finding a better home isn’t about seeing more apartments. It’s about having someone help you see options you never considered.

Note: This is a fictional scenario based on common student renting experiences. The characters and specific events are invented.
body.zh:
大一结束前，Ethan 和朋友已经开始计划搬出 NYU 宿舍。

两人想得很简单：在 Manhattan 找套公寓，平摊房租，最好离学校近一点。

结果找了几个星期，现实比想象中残酷。

预算内的房子不是太小，就是条件一般。好不容易看中一套，刚准备预约看房，就发现已经租出去了。

更崩溃的是，房租只是开始。水电、网络、各种入住费用加起来，每个月的开销比预计高出不少。

宿舍退房日期越来越近，他们却连住哪个区都没决定。

“谁说在纽约上学，就一定要住纽约？”

联系 USWOO 后，Agent 没有立刻发来一堆房源，而是先问了他们的预算、课程安排和通勤习惯。

聊到最后，Agent 突然问了一句：

“你们考虑过 Jersey City 吗？”

Ethan 第一反应是拒绝。

“我在 NYU 上学，为什么要住 New Jersey？”

但当 Agent 把 Manhattan 和 Jersey City 的房源、价格、交通路线放在一起比较时，他开始动摇了。

原来，从 Jersey City 的部分 PATH 车站出发，到 Manhattan 并没有想象中那么麻烦。

而且在相近预算下，他们可能有机会租到空间更宽敞、设施更完善的公寓。

原本以为自己是在预算和居住体验之间二选一，没想到还有第三种选择。

真正让他改主意的，是那次看房

周末，Ethan 和朋友决定去 Jersey City 实地看看。

从 PATH 车站出来，走进几栋之前从没关注过的公寓，他们才发现，河对岸的生活和想象中很不一样。

明亮的公共空间、健身房，还有部分公寓能看到的 Manhattan Skyline。

当然，Agent 也提醒他们，不能只看房子漂亮。

从公寓到 PATH 要走多久？晚上回家方不方便？算上交通费，每个月实际能省多少？

比较了几套房源和完整的通勤路线后，他们最终选定了一套靠近 PATH 的公寓。

不是因为它最豪华，而是因为预算、通勤和居住条件，终于达到了他们想要的平衡。

原来，住在纽约和生活在纽约，是两回事

搬到 Jersey City 后，Ethan 还是照常去 NYU 上课，周末和朋友在 Manhattan 聚会。

只不过，现在每天回家的路上，他会从河对岸看见熟悉的纽约天际线。

几个月前，他还觉得住在 New Jersey 是一种妥协。

现在回头看，他反而庆幸当时有人多问了一句：

“为什么一定要住 Manhattan？”

有时候，找到更合适的家，不是看了更多房子，而是有人帮你看到了原本没考虑过的选择。

注：本文为根据常见学生租房经历创作的情景案例，人物与具体经历均为虚构。

title.en: Before graduation, the most stressful part wasn’t finals. It was moving.
title.zh: 毕业前最崩溃的不是 Final 而是搬家

summary.en: His lease was ending and his new home wasn’t set. The unexpected help came from a rental agent he’d known for years.
summary.zh: 房子快到期了，新家还没着落。Daniel 怎么也没想到，最后帮他解围的，竟然是几年前认识的租房 Agent。

body.en:
Three weeks before graduation, Daniel’s life had become chaos.

Finals weren’t over, and his New York lease was about to expire. His graduate program in Philadelphia was confirmed, but his new apartment still wasn’t settled.

He finally found an apartment he liked, only to discover that the move-in date he needed didn’t line up with the building’s availability.

Meanwhile, moving company quotes came in much higher than expected. His room was full of unpacked boxes, and his phone held a long list of unanswered messages.

What made it worst was that graduation, moving out and the move itself all had to happen on time. None of them could wait.

One message changed everything

One night, Daniel was scrolling through his contacts when he suddenly thought of someone.

In his sophomore year, when he first rented in New York, he had found his agent through USWOO.

Even though that apartment search had ended long ago, the two had stayed in touch on and off.

They shared new restaurants in the city, caught up now and then, and messaged each other whenever a rental question came up. Over time, the relationship had grown from client and advisor into friendship.

Daniel had only meant to vent about the chaos of moving after graduation and maybe ask for advice.

To his surprise, his agent told him that Hi NY offered moving and settling-in support.

It turned out that leaving New York was something he didn’t have to handle alone, either.

More than an apartment, there was a whole home to move

With a direction set, Daniel began tackling the problems one by one.

Which furniture was worth bringing to Philadelphia? Which should be sold or given away? How far ahead should an intercity move be booked? When should Wi-Fi and renter’s insurance be arranged for the new place?

With Hi NY’s resources, he gradually mapped out the moving process and started lining up each task with his move-out and move-in dates.

Packing was still something he had to do himself, and plenty of small problems still popped up.

But at least he no longer had to search the internet from scratch every time something came up.

This time, it really is goodbye to New York

In the last week before graduation, Daniel finally had most of his room packed up.

Looking at the emptying apartment, he suddenly remembered how he had first moved in during his sophomore year.

Back then, he had just left the dorms and knew nothing about renting in New York.

Now, years later, he was about to take a house full of belongings to another city and start graduate school.

Before leaving, he sent his agent a message, talking about how much had changed over the years.

He had once asked for help renting a single apartment. Years later, he could still turn to the same person when it was time to leave New York.

Next stop, Philadelphia.

Note: This is a fictional scenario based on common student experiences of moving between cities. The characters and specific events are invented.
body.zh:
距离毕业还有三周，Daniel 的生活已经乱成一团。

Final 还没结束，纽约的租约就快到期了。费城的研究生项目已经确定，但新房迟迟没有着落。

好不容易看中一套公寓，询问后才发现，想要的入住日期根本对不上。

另一边，搬家公司报价比预期高出不少。房间里堆着没打包的行李，手机里还有一长串未回复的消息。

最崩溃的是，毕业、退租、搬家，哪一件都没法往后拖。

一条消息，事情有了转机

某天晚上，Daniel 翻着手机通讯录，突然想起了一个人。

大二那年，他从学校宿舍搬出来，第一次在纽约租房，就是通过 USWOO 认识了那位 Agent。

后来虽然租房的事情早已结束，两人却一直断断续续保持联系。

偶尔分享纽约的新餐厅，聊聊近况，遇到租房问题也会互相发消息。从最初的客户和顾问，慢慢成了朋友。

这次 Daniel 原本只是想吐槽一下毕业搬家的混乱，顺便问问有没有建议。

没想到，对方告诉他，USWOO 的 Hi NY 还有搬家及生活安置相关的服务资源。

原来，离开纽约这件事，也可以找老朋友帮忙。

房子之外，还有一整个家要搬

确定了方向，Daniel 终于开始一件件解决问题。

哪些家具值得带去费城？哪些不如直接处理掉？跨城搬家需要提前多久预约？新家的网络和租客保险什么时候安排？

借助 Hi NY 的相关资源，他逐渐理清了搬家流程，也开始按照退租和入住日期安排各项事项。

当然，打包还是得自己来，临时冒出来的小问题也一个没少。

但至少，不再是每遇到一件事，就从头上网搜索一次。

这次，真的要和纽约说再见了

毕业前最后一周，Daniel 终于把房间收拾得差不多了。

看着逐渐空下来的公寓，他突然想起大二第一次搬进来时的样子。

那时，他刚从宿舍搬出来，对纽约租房一窍不通。

几年过去，他已经要带着满屋子的东西，去另一个城市开始研究生生活。

临走前，他还给那位 Agent 发了条消息，聊起这些年的变化。

当初只是找人帮忙租套房，没想到几年后，连离开纽约都还能找他商量。

下一站，费城。

注：本文为根据常见学生跨城搬家经历创作的情景案例，人物与具体经历均为虚构。

title.en: I only wanted a new place. I didn’t expect my life to change too.
title.zh: 本来只是想换个房没想到生活也跟着变了

summary.en: After three years in New York, Lena discovered that a new home can bring more than a new address.
summary.zh: 在纽约生活三年，Lena 第一次发现，换个住处可能带来的不只是新的生活环境。

body.en:
In her third year in New York, Lena began to seriously consider moving.

Work was getting busier, and her schedule clashed more and more with her roommate’s. Her commute took nearly an hour each way, and she had to be careful not to disturb anyone when she got home.

She wanted to live on her own, but she didn’t want to give up the convenience of Manhattan.

The original plan was simple: find a studio within budget, ideally closer to the office.

She didn’t expect that this move would also change her social circle in New York.

One viewing, and a conversation about more than apartments

Through a friend, Lena connected with an agent at USWOO.

During viewings, the two talked about more than rent, layouts and commutes.

When the conversation turned to work, Lena mentioned that she had always wanted to meet more people in her field, but since graduating, her circle had grown smaller and more fixed.

Her days were a routine of office, subway and home, with the occasional weekend catch-up with a few friends. She lived in New York, yet her life felt smaller and smaller.

After listening, the agent mentioned that USWOO often works with young professionals from different industries, and that there are community events and networking opportunities.

Lena didn’t give it much thought at the time. After all, she had only come to find an apartment.

The apartment was found, but the connection didn’t end there

Lena moved into her new apartment.

Her commute was shorter, she could finally sleep in on weekends, and she had a living room that was truly her own.

To her surprise, her relationship with the agent didn’t end when the lease was signed.

In one conversation, the agent invited her to an industry networking event.

She went expecting only to meet a few new people, but she ended up connecting with several professionals working in related fields.

The conversation moved from work experience to industry trends, and everyone quickly exchanged contact information.

One of them later shared a career opportunity she had never considered before.

She never expected that the person she met while looking for an apartment would open the door to resources beyond her existing circle.

In New York, where you live matters, and so does who you know

A few months after moving, Lena’s life felt different.

She was still busy with work, but her weekends no longer revolved around the same few friends. Now and then she went to industry events and met new faces.

The job opportunity she heard about didn’t immediately change her career path, but it got her rethinking her future.

She had assumed the move was simply about making her life more comfortable.

In the end, what changed was not just her address, but her connection to the city.

New York has never run out of opportunities. Sometimes, what’s missing is just one chance to meet someone new.

Note: This is a fictional scenario created for illustration. The characters, events and activities are invented and do not represent any real client receiving a job opportunity.
body.zh:
在纽约的第三年，Lena 开始认真考虑搬家。

工作越来越忙，和室友的作息越来越合不来。每天通勤将近一小时，回到家还得小心翼翼地不打扰别人。

她想一个人住，但又舍不得 Manhattan 的便利。

最初的计划很简单：找个预算内的 Studio，最好能离公司近一点。

没想到，这次搬家，后来还改变了她在纽约的社交圈。

一次看房，聊出了房子以外的事

通过朋友介绍，Lena 认识了 USWOO 的 Agent。

看房时，两人聊的不只有租金、户型和通勤。

聊到工作，Lena 提起自己一直想认识更多同行，却发现毕业后社交圈越来越固定。

每天公司、地铁、家，周末偶尔见几个朋友。明明住在纽约，却感觉自己的生活越来越小。

Agent 听完，顺口提起 USWOO 平时也会接触不同行业的年轻职场人，还有一些社区活动和交流机会。

Lena 当时没太放在心上。毕竟，她只是来找房子的。

房子找到了，联系却没有结束

后来，Lena 搬进了新公寓。

通勤缩短了，周末终于能睡到自然醒，也有了真正属于自己的客厅。

但让她意外的是，和 Agent 的联系并没有在签完租约后结束。

一次聊天中，对方邀请她参加了一场行业交流活动。

原本只是抱着认识新朋友的心态过去，她却遇到了几位从事相近领域的人。

从工作经验聊到行业动态，大家很快交换了联系方式。

其中一位后来还分享了一个她之前没有关注过的职业机会。

她没有想到，当初为了找房认识的人，竟然让她接触到了原本生活圈之外的资源。

在纽约，住在哪里很重要，认识谁也一样

搬家几个月后，Lena 的生活和以前不太一样了。

她依然忙着工作，但周末不再只有固定的几个朋友，偶尔也会参加行业活动，认识一些新面孔。

那次分享的工作机会没有立刻改变她的职业方向，却让她开始重新思考未来的发展。

她原本以为，这次搬家只是想让自己住得舒服一点。

结果，改变的不只有住址，还有她与这座城市的连接。

纽约从来不缺机会。有时候，差的只是一次认识新朋友的契机。

注：本文为创作的情景案例，人物、活动及具体经历均为虚构，不代表实际客户获得了相关职业机会。
